verification.note: Memorial’s sections on comparative research and the census’s origin/method/reception read, plus life opening. Argument characterization is explicitly mediated by Miller. Image of Africa is dated 1965 here but 1964 in Curtin’s contemporary AHA bibliography; latter retained.

relations.evidence_note: Named substantive reader Joseph C. Miller’s 2009 account of the census’s origin, uncertainty and later archival responses. No fresh reading of the census or audit of modern SlaveVoyages totals; counting is not a substitute for enslaved experience.

relations.relationship: Develops comparative questions around recurring cross-cultural trade, migration, plantations and disease.
relations.evidence_note: Miller’s substantive account supplies the methodological characterization; the publisher record supports title/date only. A specific comparative agenda, not the claim that one historian founded all global history or a causal affiliation arrow.
